SCEPTRE refactor handoff

Source: vignettes/articles/contributor-tools-refactor-readme.Rmd
contributor-tools-refactor-readme.Rmd

Contributing · Object model · Discovery walkthrough · Object fields

Download the readable tour ZIP, extract it and open walkthrough.html; its links open the bug appendix. No render tool is needed to read it. The tour source, appendix source and lasting architecture guide are also available. The public API and 56-slot saved-object format are preserved. The refactor adds no new inference method, storage backend or replacement QC policy. Normal numerical behavior is checked against original commit 21f9ea098b69c444a884a49bc254de711968e3b5. Reviewed bug domains and improved worker-error reporting are explicit exceptions. From a repository clone, gh pr checkout 234 selects the review branch. The validation receipt gives the final measured outcomes and source pins. The portable tour is a ready-to-read entry point for Tim.

Material to keep

Permanent package tests check current mathematical behavior, workflow results, sampling probabilities, warnings, indexing, cache reuse and supported execution modes. The older saved object is a lasting file-format input, not an old-output snapshot. Input provenance and maintenance instructions are in tests/testthat/fixtures. Current-source native safety checks live in tools/checks. The maintained diagram lives in tools/architecture.

This directory alone is temporary. It retains the tour, exact manual comparison suite and the explicit review commands below for maintainer review. Routine CI never calls it. All developer directories are excluded from R CMD build.

Full historical evidence

The complete pre-handoff tree, original specification, plans, frozen reports, raw evidence and failed attempts are preserved at the published tag refactor-evidence-2026-10-16-e1f8109. The frozen acceptance report records measured source pins, actual Nextflow/book scope and accepted resource costs. The specification remains available there. Current validation belongs to the handoff receipt; historical numerical/resource measurements retain their original commits.

787 execution/planning/evidence files were removed from the active tree after publishing that archive. This reduces the review diff; their Git history remains. After maintainer acceptance, archive the final handoff tree before retiring this directory. Keep all permanent tests, input recipes, native checks and architecture material. Remove this directory’s links from contributor guidance at retirement.

Compare original and current SCEPTRE

Use a committed checkout, a C++ toolchain and the package dependencies. Install pkgbuild, pkgload, testthat, digest and jsonlite in your developer library. For backed qualification, follow the permanent README’s exact guarded ondisc installation; set R_LIBS to that library and require it explicitly:

R_LIBS=/absolute/dependency-library SCEPTRE_REQUIRE_ONDISC=true \
  Rscript --vanilla tools/refactor/compare.R /absolute/fresh/comparison-output

Without ondisc, in-memory comparisons run and backed tests skip; the report states that scope. An installed unqualified ondisc is rejected before running its kernels. An optional second argument selects a candidate Git ref; HEAD is the default and uncommitted changes are excluded. Output must be a fresh directory outside this checkout. The command archives both refs, freshly installs the candidate and runs the verified original in a separate process. Read comparison.json, checks.csv and the retained logs. Failures return nonzero and record a failed status, stage and error. No candidate output regenerates an expected result. This command does not qualify performance or actual Nextflow.

Read or reproduce the illustrated tour

The handoff includes a portable tour ZIP: download, extract and open walkthrough.html; keep bug-fixes.html beside it. Both pages embed their images/scripts and link source excerpts to the recorded Git commit. The ZIP’s READ-ME.txt and render.json identify that source and render tool. To reproduce it, install Quarto, R packages knitr and jsonlite, and the zip command, then run:

Rscript --vanilla tools/refactor/render.R /absolute/fresh/tour-output

The optional second argument again selects a committed Git ref. Rendering reads snippets from an immutable archive; it does not load an installed SCEPTRE or run the comparison. Authoring directly with quarto render walkthrough.qmd remains possible, but that renders the working checkout. Editable diagram sources are Graphviz .dot files. Rendered working HTML is ignored; the compact handout ZIP is retained for review and is excluded from the package.

Adversarial test check

The explicit command below checks genuine current outputs first, then verifies that nine deliberately wrong outputs are rejected by their intended assertions. It exercises the same helpers used in permanent tests and does not alter the package or any expected fixture:

Rscript --vanilla tools/refactor/check-test-strength.R /absolute/installed-library /absolute/fresh/check-output

Follow-up ownership and acceptance

Eugene, as Lead Maintainer, owns triage of the bounded accepted costs in #235 and dependency-release coordination in #236. Neither acceptance authorizes larger resource costs or enables backed CRT. An inherited numerical edge case discovered during handoff is separately tracked in #237: fully tied two-sided empirical tails can exceed one. Its original statistical formula is preserved in this refactor; the new probability-bound tests concern the nondegenerate toy workflow inputs. Eugene owns scientific triage of that separate correction. Existing scientific and pipeline roadmap work stays separate: mixture replacement #220, pairwise QC #225, and pipeline plotting timothy-barry/sceptre-pipeline#6. The final handoff also freshly executes all 30 original and candidate pipeline R-script stages; their ordered payloads match exactly. This checks actual standard/nuclear phase scripts, distinct from the earlier full Nextflow run. Inherited nuclear-script options and the book example are owned for triage in #238. The recorded book qualification is selected cells (14/15, with the inherited empty-barcode failure); pipeline qualification uses matched local arrival/seed settings. Full-book, container/array/hosted-scheduler validation belongs to their maintainers’ next qualification work, not a new feature promise from this PR.

Maintainer review of the final diff precedes merge/release. No one has been messaged, assigned a review, or represented as having approved the refactor by this handoff. This is the reproducible, reviewable delivery prepared for that step.
